title: Artificial neural network analysis links immersion with self-efficacy in VR upper-limb training
summary: Artificial neural networks analyzed self-reports from 280 healthy adults who used a VR upper-limb training system. With ten-fold cross-validation, the ANN analysis ranked immersion above learning motivation as a predictor of task-specific self-efficacy, while linear structural-equation analysis ranked learning motivation higher. This preprint reports associations in young adults from one city, without causal evidence or rehabilitation outcomes.

evidence.tested: ANN models used immersion, learning motivation, interactive experience, and perceived incentives to predict affective trust and task-specific self-efficacy; the study reports 10-fold cross-validation and RMSE. The underlying data are self-reports from 280 users.
evidence.unknown: All participants had normal upper-limb function, were aged 18–35 and came from one city. No causal effect or clinical rehabilitation improvement was tested. The manuscript inconsistently describes the system as immersive/non-immersive.
evidence.ai_role: The ANN analysis modeled nonlinear relationships among survey constructs and identified immersion as the strongest predictor of task-specific self-efficacy, complementing PLS-SEM and necessary configuration analysis.

source_review.scope: Research Square v1 full-text PDF: abstract, participant Methods, ANN analysis, cross-validation and limitations; Crossref version/publication metadata.
